set.typical_award_size: Deferral, not waiver. Under Ordinance No. 1690 (adopted June 21, 2022, no expiration date) residential infill projects (single-family or multifamily on vacant or underutilized parcels in urbanized areas) may defer ten City impact and capacity fees (General City, Library, Police, Water Capacity, Roads, Administration, Storm Drain, Fire, Wastewater, Parks) under a recorded fee deferral agreement and lien; deferred fees are due at the earlier of the final inspection request or 12 months, at the rate in effect at permit issuance. Spring Lake Infrastructure Fees, permit and plan check fees and non-City fees are not deferrable. Approval by the City Manager or Council depending on amount. The Council has also approved case-by-case interest-free deferral to just before certificate of occupancy for affordable projects (Housing Element). The Prohousing application cites Vista Del Robles (72 units, 2024) as a user.
set.affordability_requirement: None for the general program; affordable projects may also get case-by-case Council deferrals.
set.cycle_notes: Ongoing program; apply to Community Development before permit issuance. Ordinance 1690 has no sunset (replaced the 2008 program that ran through June 30, 2022).
set.next_deadline: Rolling, no deadline as of November 8, 2026. Apply through Community Development, (530) 661-5820.
set.layering_notes: Deferral improves construction-period cash flow but is not a subsidy; combine with the density bonus fee waiver incentive and Fund 1327 loans. Woodland was designated Prohousing by HCD in 2025 (application March 21, 2025), which adds Prohousing points in state programs. Spring Lake has its own financing plan; Spring Lake Infrastructure Fees cannot be deferred.

reason: Current program is Ordinance 1690 (June 21, 2022) with no sunset and 12-month deferral, and Woodland is Prohousing designated, contrary to the record.

set.typical_award_size: Small. The FY 2021/22 SB 341 report (dated August 1, 2022, the latest posted) shows a Housing Asset Fund ending balance of $51,025 cash (one loan payoff), no real property, five rental loans outstanding totaling $4,123,722 and seven first-time homebuyer loans totaling $674,693 (principal and interest through June 30, 2022). Unencumbered funds were under $1 million, so no excess surplus. Any future money comes only from loan repayments.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. No later SB 341 report is posted; ask Housing staff for the current balance.
set.layering_notes: Useful negative information: Woodland's post-RDA housing money is the inclusionary Fund 1327, not the successor fund, which held about $51,000 in cash at June 30, 2022. Rental loan repayments could add a small extremely low income layer over time. The SB 341 report is a scanned PDF; it was read page by page as images.

reason: SB 341 report read: FY 2021/22 balance $51,025 cash plus about $4.8 million in outstanding loans and no excess surplus.
